checked.found: Eridu founded c. 5400 BC (Ubaid), remembered as Sumer's oldest city

Temples date to c. 3500 BC, but the great city wall is dated to the Jemdet Nasr period (c. 3100-2900 BC); the Met puts Uruk as the largest settlement by c. 3200 BC. 'Walled' at the 3500 date is not supported. Consider dropping 'walled' from the description (and the slug).
checked.suggestion: Uruk grew into an urban centre with great temples and thousands of residents, the largest settlement of its day.

checked.found: Proto-cuneiform at Uruk c. 3350-3200 BC; 3200 conventional
Royal Tombs c. 2600-2500 BC, lyres, gold headdresses, attendants
Urukagina reforms c. 2380-2340 BC; c. 2350 within range; often called the first recorded reform
Enheduanna, daughter of Sargon, c. 2300 BC, first named author
Reign c. 2254-2218 BC; the stele itself is dated variously c. 2254-2218, c. 2250 or c. 2200. 2254 is the start of the reign, within the window.
Elamites sacked Ur and captured Ibbi-Sin c. 2004 BC (middle chronology)
Sumu-abum founded the first dynasty of Babylon c. 1894 BC (middle chronology)
Plimpton 322 c. 1800 BC (range 1822-1784), Pythagorean-triple-like number sets
Code c. 1754 BC, 282 laws on a black diorite stele
Mursili I sacked Babylon c. 1595 BC (middle chronology), took Marduk's statue, ended Hammurabi's dynasty
Ashur-uballit I accession 1365 BC (Britannica; Wikipedia c. 1363), Amarna letter to the pharaoh, ended Mitanni overlordship
Standard Babylonian version compiled between 1300 and 1000 BC; c. 1100 is an approximate midpoint (Sin-leqi-unninni)
Inauguration feast of Kalhu 879 BC, about 69,574 guests
Systematic records conventionally begin under Nabonassar, 747 BC; earliest surviving diary is 652 BC, so 747 is the start of the tradition, not of surviving tablets
Seized the throne in 745 BC after a revolt, reformed army and provinces
Palace Without Rival completed c. 691 BC, with aqueduct and gardens
Succeeded Esarhaddon in 669 BC (some sources 668); scribal training attested
Battle of Carchemish 605 BC, Nebuchadnezzar (then crown prince) defeated Egyptians and Assyrian remnant on the Euphrates
